utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to all the people present here, representatives of the OTP, Defence counsel, and accused. In a few moments we're going to have a new witness, but before he comes in, let me say this: Yesterday, Mr. Praljak forwarded to the Trial Chamber a document in which he asked for some questions to be put to the witness. I gave this paper an IC number. I remind you that if you wish to communicate with the Trial Chamber on behalf of an accused, you must forward it to the counsel who can forward the document further on or intervene already or can rise at any moment to put the question if it is his turn to do so or because he wants to change anything to the transcript, because he saw there was a mistake in it or because he has something important to say. Regarding the next witness, as you know, I told you that the Prosecution would have one hour for the direct examination and one hour and a half [Realtime transcript read in error "one hour"] for the Defence. Further to the Rules, I conduct, control the way witnesses are heard in order to avoid any waste of time. I would like to they will to Mr. Praljak, because I suppose he's going to ask questions of the witness. I tell him that the witness is going to testify as to what he saw on the 8th of December whilst -- sorry. Sorry. I misspoke. On the 8th of November, whilst the bridge fell on the next day, on the 9th of November. So this witness is going to speak about tank fire on the 8th of November. Regarding the 9th of November, the Prosecutor intends to submit certain documents to the witness, and I saw in them that several of them were signed by (redacted), who is mentioned as a possible Prosecution witness in the 65 ter list. If the said witness is going to testify, and I see no reason why he shouldn't, you could ask relevant questions of that witness as to what happened on the 9th of November and to give you a full picture and to avoid any sort of side-tracking, I remind you that through previous witnesses another document was introduced mentioning proceedings against the three tank soldiers who were manning the tank. Remember, we have a document mentioning this. In a few moments, during cross-examination, I would like Mr. Kovacic to tell me -- whether through his questions or through the answers, tell me exactly what Mr. Praljak's position was on the 8th or 9th of November. Indeed, we received evidence indicating that Mr. Praljak had left his office early November, and I don't know exactly when he left that position. If he did so on the 9th of November, on that day, on the 9th of November, he could not have played any part in the firing that took place on that day. So this should be clarified for the sake of the Trial Chamber to specify when Mr. Praljak left office in November, since we know that he did so in that month, in November 1993. This is what I wanted to convey to you to the extent that I am under the obligation of conducting the way the testimony is going to take place, which was specified in an appeals decision in the Jean-Paul Akayseu case. The Appeals Chamber, in response to the seventh ground of appeal the defendant, said that the Presiding Judge has the duty, the duty, the obligation to control the way in which a witness is heard. I will now ask for the witness to be brought in, for him to make the solemn declaration. In the meantime, registrar, can you give me a number, an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We've received the Office of the Prosecutor's response to Mr. Stojic's objection to the admission of exhibits relating to the witness Finlayson, and that will be IC 562.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, just a small point. On the transcript this morning -- this afternoon, rather, it shows that Your Honour said one hour for Prosecution, one hour for Defence. I think Your Honour's have in mind an hour and a half, which is what you said yesterday for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to clear that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Yes. I did not divide the time among the teams because I thought you would do it yourselves, but failing an agreement, it seems logical for Mr. Praljak to have 40 minutes and for the remainder of the time to be split among the other teams. So 10 minutes for each team. You could also decide to devote your time or give your time away to Mr. Praljak, if you so wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry for having delay your testimony. You had to wait all day yesterday. We thought you could start yesterday, but due to problems related to the previous witness it was not possible to do so, so please accept our apologies. Can you please state your first name, surname, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Enes Delalic. I was born on the 1st of August, 1956, in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your occupation, your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a professional driver. Now I work as a guard. I am attached to the same company that I used to drive a bus for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, have you had an opportunity to testify before a court, a national or international court as to the events that took place in your country, or is this the first time you're going to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never. This is the very first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read out the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, some explanations very briefly as to the way this hearing is going to unfold. You are going to be first asked questions by the representative of the Prosecution. I suppose you have met with him already some time ago. And following this initial phase, Defence counsel or accused themselves can ask questions on cross-examination. You have four Judges in front of you. They, too, can ask questions. According to the Rules they can ask questions at any time, but we try as much as possible to do so only towards the end when everybody has asked their questions, but sometimes, exceptionally so, we do ask questions because we have to. So this is how your testimony is going to take place. Please try to it answer as precisely as possible. If at any point in time you do not feel well for any reason, please just tell us so. I'm now going to give the floor to the Prosecution, who is going to start with the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon to Your Honours and to everybody else in and about the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And good afternoon, Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I'm going to start with some background questions firstly, and I'd ask you to be as brief as possible where you can. Can you tell us simply where you were living at the very early part of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It's called Donja Mahala, Gojka Vukovica 75. That was the house and the street number.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say that Donja Mahala is situated in the city of Mostar and is situated on the right bank; that is, the west side?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's on the west bank, in the west of Mostar. On the west bank of the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And would it also be correct to say that this was an area or district which was predominantly inhabited by Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, do you remember, did a serious armed conflict break out as between Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats in Mostar in or around May 9th, 1993, lasting well into 1994?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did this conflict result in the establishment of confrontation lines within the city of Mostar between the protagonist forces?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just for the record, what were the Bosnian Croat forces known as?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, your district, Donja Mahala, was it located to the confrontation lines between the protagonist forces?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No. It was under the control of the BH army, this part of Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And where was the nearest confrontation line to it?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: The nearest line was exactly where my flat was, which was the last, deepest line.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And after the conflict began did you and your family remain residing in Donja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It wasn't possible for reasons of safety. I had two children and a wife. I was a member of the police units myself; therefore, it wasn't possible for me to stay there. My father lived on the west bank, and there was the bridge between us. So I moved my children to my father's flat at Tekija to stay with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And when did you move your family there? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Right after the first clashes erupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, did all the Bosnian Muslims living in Donja Mahala, did they move to East Mostar or did they stay in Donja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No. Not all of them had the same opportunity that I did, unfortunately. They stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Were there some that moved to the other bank voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Not voluntarily. They were driven by their trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you originally were living in Donja Mahala and you moved to this Tekija. With the permission of the Court, could I show you a photograph which doesn't form part of the exhibit bundle but which -- copies of which I have made, hard copies, available to the Court and to my colleagues on the Defence, and perhaps just so that we can orientate ourselves, perhaps you could tell us if you recognise the photo, if you see your house -- or your own apartment, and if you see the place where you moved your family to.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO, if it's possible. I will need an IC number for this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be IC 563.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If you could move it --

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Can you point out to the Trial Chamber where your apartment is or was at the time the conflict started?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Right here. That's my flat. At the top of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put an X on it for us.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Right there. In the attic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us where you moved to? Can you see the area which you moved to on the map? I think if you move it over to the right you may come to it.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If we could move the photograph. It's slightly out -- out of view from the ELMO. Move it a little bit more. A little bit more. A little bit more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Could you put an A where you say your father's flat was.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you see the area in the foreground of the photograph? It's an elevated position. Do you -- it's almost across the road from your own house. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That is Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: That is Stotina. Now --

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Infamous Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, you told us you were a police officer. Could you tell us where you were working and whether or not you went to your work every day from your home -- from your temporary home in Tekija?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And where did you go to work? Where was your work location situated?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I took a street called Santiceva Street, and that's where the police station was, in the Partizan cinema building.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I think that's located far off into the centre of the city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's in the centre of the city near the Musala bridge. It used to be called Marsal Tito's bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, even though you were living in Tekija, did you ever return to your apartment during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes. I occasionally returned to just check on my flat and see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say that one would be able to see the activity on Stotina hill from your apartment?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. It wasn't really a relaxed viewing, so to speak, but if you tried hard you could have an open view, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who occupied the hill of Stotina during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It was HVO controlled. It was controlled by the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you personally see HVO troops there on the hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, occasionally. I sometimes used a pair of binoculars, and sometimes I would get my camera to film something in the heat of the moment, so to speak, but very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I mean, how would you have known they were HVO? Could you give us a brief description of what you saw? How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, there were those wearing black uniforms, those wearing camouflage uniforms, and they all displayed HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you ever have an opportunity to see any military activity on the hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: They had a bunker at Stotina. They would go there, and they used that position to fire at the west bank, and they didn't let anyone go by.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And when you say when they fired at the west bank, what were they firing with?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: All sorts of weapons that they had, rifles, tanks, anti-aircraft guns. All sorts of things. Whatever they had. They used whatever they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Over the past month or so the panel had some -- had quite a considerable amount of evidence presented to it to the effect that there was sniping coming from the hill of Stotina. Now, I don't need to go into any detail, but could you simply confirm that there was indeed sniping coming from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Everybody knows it, don't they? There's no need to confirm something like that, but if you want me to, I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, these people who were still living in Donja Mahala during the conflict, how did they maintain contact with the people living on the other bank?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, via the bridges, the bridges that were still left. Actually, they had all been destroyed with the exception of the Old Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And apart from the Old Bridge was there any other bridge that the people on the west bank and the east bank would use to keep in contact?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes. Our own army made a bridge called the Kamenica bridge, and then there was another bridge called Tenzin Bridge, and then there was the Old Bridge, and further down we had the Tito Bridge, which the UNHCR had put up. It was a provisional bridge. But that one was damaged, too, later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So for the record, who was in control of the Stari Most and the Kamenica bridge?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: The Bosnian forces, we.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, you spoke about this military activity that you witnessed in Stotina and the firing that came from Stotina. Apart from the sniping, did you have -- did you ever have an opportunity to witness firing from Stotina from any heavier weapons?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I did. There was a tank demolishing the bridge, and I certainly remember that quite clearly. And anti-aircraft guns were used too. There was one being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Can you remember what date this happened on? Can you describe to us what happened?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I filmed the tank on the 8th of November --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: -- sometime. 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And what time did you start to film the tank? Can you remember approximately?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Sometime about 10.30. Thereabouts. I can't quite remember specifically. It was a long time ago. But there's the footage and it's self-explanatory. It's all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Before we go to that, can you tell us how it was that it came to your attention that there was a tank firing from Stotina, and where you were at that particular time and what you actually did?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: That day I was at home. It was my day off. Prior to that, I had been at work. Sometime the previous night I arrived back home. The next morning I heard a tank firing. It was nearby. I was in my flat at Tekija. This piqued my curiosity and since there was sufficient time for me to go and film, at first I tried to observe a little lest I should lose any footage. I wanted to be sure that I would take a good shot of it and to see where it was positioned and where it was firing from.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And how was it that you knew specifically where the tank was?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a lady neighbour of mine across from where I lived, and she was the one I asked. Quite simply, I asked, "Where's this coming from?" I could hear it nearby but I couldn't see it. I could hear the sound coming from Stotina. I couldn't spot the tank right away, though. I was also afraid of snipers. So at first I looked around to see that it was safe, and she said that, "Don't tell me you can't see it. There's a tank right there. It's Stotina." "All right, Stotina," I said, but I couldn't spot it right away. I just heard the sound of a tank firing, which is a familiar sound. You know what a tank sounds like, and you know what other weapons sound like when firing. At one point I did spot it. I grabbed my camera, and I got ready to film. At first I could tell by the sound that it was nearby. I set my camera up, and my neighbour was telling me, "Can't you see it? Can't you see it?" She must have been the first to stop spot it. She said, "Can't you see?" So I climbed a chair to get a better view and I finally spotted, noticed the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Where exactly were you when you had the camera on you climbed on the chair? Were you in your own apartment?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No. I was in my neighbour's apartment, and her name was Mejra Hadzic. And her daughter was there, too, in the apartment, Zejna Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I see. Sorry for interrupting. If you could continue. You had just climbed onto the chair.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and that's when I started filming. I zoomed in to make it closer. I was looking at it, but I was afraid because there was sniper firing from the neighbouring house from time to time. So I didn't want him to hit me, and I didn't want to cause any harm to myself, so I did it carefully. And at one point I saw the tank, and I saw the firing coming out of the tank as it fired. So I zoomed in, filmed it, and keep the tape as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, as you climb onto the chair and you began to zoom in on the location where the tank was, can you tell us: What direction were you pointing your camera in?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I pointed it in the direction of Stotina, which is where the tank was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And as you were filming, did you have an opportunity to see any of its crew?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: You say that you saw it firing. Can you tell us how many times you saw it firing during the period that you were filming?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now, but it was 10 to 15 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did you speak to your neighbour as -- at the same time as you were filming?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. We discussed it for a while, and then we listened to the news over the radio as well to see what they were saying, to see whether it was the bridge that was being targeted. So our people were broadcasting that over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: When you say "the radio," you mean the public radio?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the public radio. And they played music on the radio, too, for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And as you were watching this tank, did you note whether or not it fired in the same direction all the time, or can you tell us if it changed direction?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, what I noticed was only in one direction. It did move around and make moves forward and backwards, but it was always the same direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Were you in a position to see what it was firing at from the location from where you were filming?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, from where I was filming I couldn't see that, but it was quite obvious. You knew where he would be firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Were you able to see any evidence at all anywhere in the direction to which it was firing, that it might have hit anything?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't actually see that, but I did see that the barrel was turned in the direction of the Old Bridge, and I heard over the radio, too, reports that it was targeting the foundations of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, did there come a stage when this tank stopped firing and, if so, when was that, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It was sometime around evening or about 5.00. It was a long time ago. I can't remember everything, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you say you started filming in the morning. The tank stopped firing in the evening. Were you filming all the way through?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Well, not the whole time, actually, because my camera couldn't film for a long time, but I did film the most important moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: When the tank stopped -- stopped firing, do you remember whether or not it had become dark or whether it was still bright?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, it was still daylight. When I stopped filming - my battery expired, and then I had to stop - but it carried on firing. Not for a long time after that, and then it was silent afterwards, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you at any stage after the firing had -- had ceased, try to find out exactly what it had been firing at or confirmed -- confirmed for yourself that -- that it had hit anything?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I learnt that the next day, where it was shooting at, what it was shooting at, because I listened to the news. So I knew it that day. I knew it was the direction, so I wasn't wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And taking the next day, the 9th of November, 1993, can you remember did you either hear or see the tank again on that day, or had it ceased completely?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It fired the next day, too, but I had to go to work to take up my shift. I called it my job, my work, but it was a shift, actually, that I was doing. And so I stayed at work. But I did happened to notice at around half past 10.00 or 11.00 that there was heavy shooting, strong firing, and I wondered what it was. The tank is firing all the time. It's just firing and firing. And some people were even crying, and I wondered what was happening, and they said, "Well, the Old Bridge has fallen." And I said, "Well, that can't be possible." And they said,"Yes." So the day before I had seen this tank firing, and the tank demolished the bridge, and that's what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And when you -- did you actually see the bridge fall yourself with your own eyes from where you were?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't see it fall, but on my way back I saw that the bridge wasn't standing any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did anything significant happen on the 9th of November to indicate that the bridge had fallen?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Of course. They were rejoicing. They were shooting all over the place. It was general merriment when they demolished the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, when you started to film was there a clock on the screen of your video recording the time?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a clock which recorded the time, but I had to turn the clock back. So it was the old time that I had, and I didn't adjust it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So during the time -- during the period you were filming, it wasn't actually realtime? How far was it out? How far had you to adjust it?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't realtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: How much did you have to adjust it?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: An hour exactly, one hour. Well, you had to set the clock back, as you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you save video which you had taken of the tank firing and keep it after the war?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did keep it, precisely so I could have it as evidence if I ever needed it, and then I offered it to The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So in 19 -- in 2006, on learning that you had the tape, did the ICTY contact you, and did you hand over the tape to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, of my own free will. And I was in a daily called the Daily Avaz. An article came out about me. I think it came out on the 17th of May, so that people called me up, but I just decided to give to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did you make any alterations or changes to the clip relating to the 8th of November, 1993, before giving it to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. The cassette wasn't -- the cassette wasn't touched. It's the original one. It's the same one that I took out of the camera, and it's like that today as it was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to my question about the video clock, for your information, you will know this obviously, the clip relating to the 8th of November on the original tape started at 1100 hours. So if the screen showed 1100 hours on your video, what was the actual real time?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, that should have been 10.00 then, and that's quite certain. I think that on the video I actually say that. I utter those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And similarly, the video closes for the 8th of November in or around the -- 16.57. Can I take it, therefore, that the real time would have been approximately 15.57?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, at this stage I'd like to show you a video extract from Exhibit P 09889, which is an extract from video 7035, which is the video that you handed to the ICTY. And if you look at your monitor, we will play the video, and then I will ask you a few short questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Can you see the fire? I can hear it but can't see it. "Mejra: There it is, at Stotka. "Enes: I'd like to see it. You can see it, hear it working. It's targeting the Old Bridge. "Mejra: It's targeting the foundation. "Enes: Can you see where it's coming from? [No interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, do you recognise this videotape?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And the scenes that we played. Is this a part of the video that you presented to the --

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I do recognise it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And is this a part of the video that you presented to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And can you confirm to us, is that you speaking during the filming?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And is that the neighbour whose name you mentioned to us earlier on?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like, for the record, to be -- it noted that the tank was seen or heard on the video clip that we showed for the period the 8th of November, 1993, that's the Exhibit P 09889, to have fired on one occasion between 16.53 and 16.54, once between 16.54 and 16.55, once between 16.55 and 15 -- 16.56, twice between 16.56 and 16.57, and twice between 16.57 and 16.58. And I'm explain to you the reasons later.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, you mentioned briefly -- I beg you pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I might be allowed to say something with regard to the record and transcript as to what was seen on the video. I have a comment to make. First of all, the video will probably be tendered and everybody will be able to judge what can be seen on the tape, but I for one, perhaps I'm wrong, but I never saw the tank, as my learned friend is observing. We heard shooting. It can be a tank, but it need not. So once again, that observation must be assessed and appraised. And now some additional explanation. We tried to view the video with the help of a better device, and we couldn't see the tank. The tank cannot be seen on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And I don't disagree with Mr. Kovacic in any way. I found it very difficult to see the tank myself. Perhaps I can ask just Mr. Delalic for one clarity question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, you saw how difficult it was to see the tank. Did you yourself see the tank with your naked eye, and can you tell it us what part of the tank you saw at any stage on the 8th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Of course I saw it. I saw the turret and the barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to avoid any misunderstanding, I did not challenge the fact that the witness saw the tank --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I shall take over. Sir, what we shall do, we shall look at the video again, and when you see the tank, say stop. Have you understood me? Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, please take a pen or pointer and tell us where it is. You don't have one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see a bit the turret. Well, this is a really small screen here. When the journalist filmed it, you could see it even better because I have a television screen which is a 72 screen. That should be the turret.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I think he'll have to use his mouse to show Your Honours. If he could come here, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not where the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, if you could come over to this screen, you can show us where it is, point the arrow at it.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: That's the tank there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that Mr. Delalic has pointed to an object in the centre of the screen, slightly raised, shaded grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, what do you -- what part of the tank do you say that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before -- Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you can challenge this during the cross-examination. I'm very surprised by this. I told you a while ago that there is an HVO document which acknowledges the fact that there was a tank there, so you are going to discuss this now and say that there was no tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I wasn't going to challenge the witness on this point. I'm just reacting to the observation made my learned friend in the transcript. He is recording what can be seen. Now, I want to state that the witness just indicated a point on the video which you can't see with the naked eye. You can't recognise it with the naked eye. That's what I wanted to observe. And I just want to have that on record, because what -- the way my learned friend characterised it is going a bit too far, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, I note that the image is inconclusive. All we can see is that before the witness said "stop," we saw the flames, and we saw a shot being fired. Whether it's a tank or a barrel or a cannon, it's very difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would suggest that we continue looking at the video, because now we are focused and maybe we see more or we see less.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only state that this is a tank. That is my conviction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we can continue to watch the videotape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw it with the naked eye. Now at some point you will see the smoke coming out. I think you can even hear the sound right now. There it is. It's firing now. This is smoke coming out of the tank's exhaust pipe, right next there to the chimney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the Bench has noticed that on two occasions we saw smoke coming out. That's quite visible on the screen. And for the record, I would also like to indicate that we can clearly see or have been able to see clearly on three occasions three shots being fired. The flames are very long and the trajectory horizontal. This is quite clear on the screen. Nonetheless, we cannot clearly see the shape of a tank because there's foliage in front. This stands in the way, and we cannot clearly see that there is a tank there. Mr. Flynn, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I think when you listen to the tape and you hear a the sound of the heavy shot from the, let's call it for the sake of argument an object, what you say is a tank, seconds before that tank fires we hear a lighter calibre weapon firing, three bursts. Do you remember that happening, and can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I have to object to this question, because I don't believe that my learned friend, or the witness, for that matter, are experts to the extent that they could judge the kind of weapon by the sound of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... right, but on listening to the tape we can hear two sounds. This is unquestionable. One sound which comes from the flames, which is quite a specific sound, but we also hear -- in the absence of the flames, we can hear a shot being fired, which is, in terms of decibels, much lower and seems to come from a much smaller weapon. This is what we can indicate as far as the sound is concerned without drawing any further conclusions thereof. Witness, you are the video-maker. We can hear two sounds. Is that what you heard also when you were there? The second sound we can hear, the sound which is more muffled, less loud, where does this sound come from? Even if you're not an expert, you perhaps have some knowledge of firearms, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's an anti-aircraft gun, most probably. I can't be certain, but it was probably providing signals for the actual firing, whether the target has been hit or not. It was actually guiding the fire of the tank. That was my understanding. It was providing guidance for the tank fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, what you've just said, this comment you've just made, and this is -- I'm during to Mr. Kovacic in order to avoid wasting any time. You say at the time you were filming you heard the comment and there was a comment which was recorded together with the tape; is that right? So what we see hear is, in fact, on the tape. The comment was made live, so to speak, at the time the person was filming -- the witness was filming. Please proceed, Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, I'd like to give you another photograph. It's an aerial photograph which the trial panel has seen previously during the testimony of Mostar witnesses and which had previously been marked, I believe, as IC 421, but perhaps a new IC number may be necessary. Do you see where your house is on that? This is an aerial photograph. Perhaps you can turn it around the other way. It might be better. Mr. Delalic, you can look at it on the ELMO itself. Do you see where your house is?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Could you point and mark with an X where your house is, please.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And across from that you have the hill of Stotina. If you could pull that into focus, please. It needs to be moved over to the left. Left. Keep -- no. Sorry, the other way. Keep going, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, you see the hill of Stotina. Can you mark on the map, if you know, where the tank was located? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Around about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And across the river is Tekija. Could you mark approximately from where you were filming. Mark that with an A, please -- sorry, with a B. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have indicated where your house was, and you indicated where the tank was. What distance is there between the house where you were filming from and the tank according to you? How many metres are there between these two spots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say exactly. It's the width of the river times three, roughly speaking, which might amount to about 800 metres or thereabouts. I really can't be more specific than that. I never measured the river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you. Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, you mentioned what happened on the 8th and the 9th. I'd like you to have a look at another two video clips which are extracts from video 2777 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all we'll give the map an exhibit number. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit IC 564.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at another two video clips which are extracts from 277 on Exhibit P 01040.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And I can tell Your Honours this was provided on the Rule 92 bis process by another witness relative to Mostar who annexed it to his statement, and in the statement he said that, "I'm handing over to you a one and a half hour video cassette that I personally recorded of different programmes broadcast by the Croatian HTV in Mostar in 1993. In the recordings there are a view of the Mostar bridge before the war and when it was destroyed." And I can confirm that this video was disclosed to the Defence in addition to the other one. If we could run both -- the first clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, that's the first clip. If we can now have the second clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. For the record, I note that at 15.52 on this video clip dated the 8th of November there is an impact on the bridge. At 15.53, a second impact on the bridge. At 15.55, third impact on the bridge. And we can see that at the time pieces of falling. You can see some water rising just at that time. It's quite visible. At 15.55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may ask a question. From which side is one looking at the bridge, from down Neretva or from up Neretva? Do you know, Witness? Does one look from the Donja Mahala side on the bridge in this video, or has it been taken from the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a view from Donja Mahala towards the bridge. From Donja Mahala. You see, you can even see the time. My camera didn't show the exact time, but now -- we need an expert to compare the two videos. It is 100 per cent accurate. I categorically state that my footage is authentic. I back my footage 100 per cent. I'm 100 per cent behind it. I've never had an opportunity to see this video like this with the time and everything, but I've seen it now. I've compared it, and if you're still not satisfied, perhaps we can get an expert to confirm it for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No. I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would complement the President says for the regard that the impacts one sees on the bridge are all to the right side of the middle of the bridge. That is, they are closing to East Mostar than to West Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be that way, or at least that's what I think, if the tank was firing from that position, and then there's the Neretva River canyon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: This was actually not a question, Witness. It was just an entry for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I thank you for the comments in relation to the times on the second bridge -- [French on English channel] ... because I was going to mention it after we had seen the second clip. But I'll ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Before we move on to the second clip, I'll ask you first, Mr. Delalic, the first the last clip you saw and you saw a number of explosions on the bridge, specifically at 15.52, 15.53, and 15.55, and in the video which you took, we saw what appears to be an object firing on a number of occasions, you say, in the direction of the bridge, including at times between 16.55 and 16.54, and 16.56 and 16.57, which in adjusted realtime would be 15.53 and 15.56, which is, significantly, the time that the explosions were seen on or against the bridge. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Even a child would know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And was there any other -- was there any other heavy weaponry that you might identify as a tank that you could hear firing at these specific times in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, no other weapon but a tank. I saw the tank myself, especially when the battery was beginning to run out and then the light began to blink, and that's when I needed it most, but I couldn't. I would have been able to take a better shot of it right then, but it was no longer possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to have a look at the second clip from this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can hear the celebratory fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: For the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, what the Bench can see is that we can see the Old Bridge, and at some point in time we see some water rising on the right-hand side without the bridge having been hit by anything. And then a few minutes later on the picture we see the Old Bridge collapsing, and at that moment we see some more water rising, which stands perpendicularly to the first water surge. So much for the record. We can look at this again, if you like. Could we see the video clip again, please? For the record, these are not conclusions. These are just things -- observations. These are just observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Everybody can see there's some water rising here on the right-hand side, a waterline, so to speak. Please continue. Whereas the Old Bridge is still standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, I would like to add two things. The first water surge we can see. We can also see that there's a lot of smoke rising from the bridge. It's not like these little puffs of smoke we saw at 15.52 and 15.55. At this point in time there's a lot of smoke. Just before the bridge collapses, we all of a sudden see the images shifting. We have the feeling that the images don't follow one another. Just before the bridge collapses, we have the feeling that the images have been switched, whether it's been filmed in realtime or not. So we wonder whether it has been filmed in a continued fashion or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: One -- could I add that one can observe that while one sees what appears to be deep crevices on the eastern part of the bridge, suddenly it is on the western side that the whole bridge vertically seems to break off the wall to which it was attached, and when it falls into the water, it looks as if there were some more explosions in the water, actually, but maybe one could watch that again, because it's quite -- quite surprising. Not easily to be explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Can you continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. I think I misobserved when I thought to see an explosion in the water after the bridge falls down.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours, the record could also reflect that at the end on the scene after the bridge has fallen into the water, it can be clearly -- shooting can be clearly be heard. That may be consistent with what the witness described as "celebratory shooting."

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, in your testimony today, you spoke of hearing the shelling or the firing starting early on the 8th of November, 1993, some hours after you came back from work. You talked later of seeing -- what you call was a tank firing what we saw regularly from Stotina in the direction of the bridge, and you said it was firing some time into the late afternoon. Can you tell us, is the Stari Most situate or adjacent to the old town? Is it situate or adjacent to the old town, the Stari Most?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It's right in the old town.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at Exhibit 0993 [sic] which you have in the book in front of you. If you turn to Exhibit 0993. And you'll find the Bosnian version at the back. Do you have it? Yeah. And this is a signed and stamped report issued by Miljenko Lasic, the HVO district commander on the 8th of November, 1993, at 1900 hours, and sent to the Main Staff, and in this report Commander Lasic reports at paragraph 2, point 1, the third part, he says "from 8.10 in the morning, our tank was opening fire from Stotina during the whole day, and it fired 50 projectiles on Stari Grad," which we know is the old town. Is Commander Lasic's report consistent with what you saw and heard on the 8th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, it's correct that it fired. He says it fired too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And after the Old Bridge was destroyed, did the HVO issue statements denying that they had deliberately destroyed the Old Bridge?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that I happened to read in the papers somewhere that Mr. Praljak was defending himself from -- saying that he didn't destroy the bridge and that he was going to prove that he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Well, that would bring me to another exhibit in the booklet that you have in front of you. Could you turn to Exhibit P 06564. Again, this is another communication -- do you have it?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: 6564. I think you have it there in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: This is another communication again written by Commander Lasic, addressed to the government and to the minister for defence and the HVO Main Staff, and it's dated the 10th of November, 1993. And in this, at paragraph 5, and if you could look at paragraph 5 for me. Commander Lasic says: "HVO units never targeted the Old Bridge and destroying it was not the aim. Defending themselves against numerous attacks by the MOS from the direction of the Old Bridge towards Podhum and the Franciscan church where there were many breakthroughs of the defence lines. Units fired at the enemy's manpower and materiel near the bridge. The old bridge was destroyed as a consequence of combat operations, because that area has been the scene of fierce clashes since the beginning of the conflict." With you aware of any offensive launched by the ABiH on either the 8th or 9th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that at all, that that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And when Commander Lasic says that they never targeted the Old Bridge and destroying it was not the aim, would you agree with what he says in this communication?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: How can I agree? I can't agree that they didn't target the Old Bridge when the Old Bridge was our lifeline, and they wanted to stifle our lifeline, let alone destroy the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Flynn, you have to finish, because you've already used your hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I have just about three questions to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Judge Prandler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: The proceedings, I would only like to make a comment, Mr. Flynn, about this document which you have of just introduced. That is the number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: 06564. It is a factual, I would say correction, I would like to make in the letter itself and -- I mean, it is not a letter, but a report. The report, paragraph four. The commander, Miljenko Lasic, mentions UNICEF twice in that paragraph four. It was probably, and I am sure that it should be read, of course, as UNESCO, because it is UNESCO who is dealing with those heritage problems, and so the reference should have been UNESCO and not UNICEF. It is just for a factual understanding. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was a direct translation from the Bosnian version, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just to try and conclude, Mr. Delalic --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: With your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did the shelling of the bridges across the Neretva by the HVO stop on the 9th of November, 1993, after the Old Bridge was knocked down?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question. You mean the shelling of the bridge or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: On -- on the 9th, Stari Most fell into the water. That left the Kamenica bridge, and my understanding is there were some other bridges farther up along the water. Did the shelling of the bridges across the river by the HVO stop on the 9th after the Stari Most was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, it did not. I think that on the cassette you can see when the Kamenica bridge was targeted too. There as something targeting Kamenica. I think it's on this video. So as far as I was able to, I filmed that, but we ought to see it on the other tape. I don't know whether you've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: We haven't presented this as part of the package because the view is not good, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: But can you tell us the date on which this would have happened?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I think it was round about the 11th of November. The 9th is when the bridge fell, and they continued, constantly hitting. Well, they had it in their minds to destroy us and that's it, but we didn't let ourselves be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And what was the direct result of the two bridges being destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, the result, the result was to cut off the approach to our homes, and then we couldn't go anywhere else. What could we do? Jump into the Neretva River? There was nothing else to do. They might have taken control of the other side, the opposite bank, and that was it. And that was their goal, to reach the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I have one last question for you. Could you turn to Exhibit 0099 -- sorry, Exhibit number 09992. Do you have that? Briefly, this is again a signed and stamped report issued by Commander Lasic of the HVO on the 9th of November, 1993, at 1900 hours, again to the Main Staff, and in paragraph 2, the second part of paragraph 2, he says, "In addition to fire from infantry weapons at around 1000 hours our tank fired a few projectiles at a target which was determined earlier. At around 10.15 hours, our reconnaissance people from Hum reported that Stari Most, the Old Bridge, was torn down, but they could not say anything about the cause of its destruction." Now, you spoke -- you said in your testimony that as far as you were aware that the Stari Most was destroyed around 10.30 to 11.00. He talks about sometime around 10.15 hours. Is this consistent with what you understand, the time the bridge was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You can see for yourself. 10.15, while it reached our ears, while we could hear what was happening, well, that would make it the right time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I said that was my last question, and it will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to have a break, and then we can start with the cross-examination for an hour and a half. We shall resume in 20 minutes' time, at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who is going to start with the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Before they do, Your Honour, could I just mention one thing? I just note from the transcript on page 31, at line 18 and 19, that when quoting the reference for a P exhibit I said P 0993. That should actually read P 09993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So there was a 9 missing. Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now turning to the Defence counsel. Sorry for taking the floor before they start. I wanted to wait until the end, but it might be better to turn to the Prosecutor right now. Mr. Prosecutor, of course I'm not a specialist in explosives, but we know that there are a lot of theories going around, around the Old Bridge, and by which weapons it was hit and also about the authors of the fire. We know from experience that explosions may be different and impacts may be different also depending on whether the projectile or the shell is made up of TNT or compressed air. Equally, if you have a shell within a building, it may cause the windowpanes to fall outside, and if you have a shell bursting outside, it would make it so that the windowpanes fallen side. So here is my question: Whilst we were viewing this footage, the Judges had questions on these lines of water or waves that rose from the river, and also on the pieces of the bridge that collapsed and fall in entire blocks. So my question is as follows: Do you have a specialist or an expert witness who could explain to us the explosions, the impacts on the bridge? Maybe if we had one we would be better able to know whether this was caused by tank fire, by what kind of tank, by what type of calibre. I don't know whether there could have been mines there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I want to supplement this question, which is a relevant one. Do you plan to call further witnesses who would speak about the destruction of the bridge? For example, about these aspects that have been raised by the Judge?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It's my understanding that there is no intention to call any expert witness to deal with the actual cause of destruction of the Old Bridge. The intention of the Prosecution was to present the best evidence that it had available to it, namely the evidence of the witnesses who were in Mostar on the 8th and 9th of November, 1993, and who could give evidence, indirect evidence, that there was fire directed at the bridge. Combined with that, we have presented you evidence, video footage of the destruction of the bridge on the same dates the witnesses say it was destroyed, and I'm sure when sit down and look at it, you will see that the explosions that were seen on the bridge coincide with firing of the object that Mr. Delalic saw. So it was the Prosecution's intention to rely on Mr. Delalic's evidence and the evidence of other Mostar witnesses who spoke generally about the destruction of the bridge, together with the documentary evidence that it proposes to tender in which it's clearly stated, and I think the President mentioned this at the outset of the hearing, it's clearly admitted by the HVO that their tank fired 50 projectiles from 8.10 on the morning of the 8th of November in the direction of Stari Grad, and we know that Stari Most was part of Stari Grad. So all of this evidence together, it would be the Prosecution's submission, that there could be no other conclusion but that it was this tank which was used by the HVO forces that brought the bridge down on this particular day. So in short, we don't propose to call specialist evidence to say that the -- that -- to describe the explosions on the bridge, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At least you have provided a clear answer. I'm now turning to the Defence. Who's going to start? Is it Mr. Praljak who's going to do all of the of cross-examination? Otherwise, you have 10 minutes each and 40 minutes for Mr. Praljak. Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in keeping with the recent ruling of yours, I don't want to take up any time. I think that you have the arguments clearly before you. Mr. Praljak has special knowledge about these events, and with your permission, I'd like to cede my time entirely to Mr. Praljak for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the entire Defence time is given to Mr. Praljak. Yes, Mr. Murphy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honour. We do not have any questions. We would be happy to give our time to General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Karnavas is replaced by Ms. Tomanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence of Mr. Prlic has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Petkovic Defence gives its time to Mr. Praljak. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] No questions for the witness so we [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Praljak. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the same view, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you shall conduct the cross-examination. You have all the parameters. You can start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. If -- just by way of an introduction. Since I've dealt with this problem for many years and it stems from a sentence stated by the witness that Praljak is proving that he didn't destroy the Old Bridge, which testifies to legislation and nowhere do you have to prove your innocence - it is the other way round - so I'd like you to interrupt me if I ask a question outside what is considered proper here. Having said that:

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Would you give short answers to my questions, as clear as possible. And if I ask you an additional question, then you can testify or you can say, "I know," "I don't know," et cetera. I think we've understood each other.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's start off with the 9th of November, 1993. When in the morning did you go to take up your duties at Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I'm always on duty as a policeman, but on that occasion I left sometime between 7.00 and 8.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Since we're on this subject, in Santiceva Street you went to the Partizan Cinema Hall; is that right? Some earlier witnesses have testified --

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, other witnesses have talked about that, but you were at the cinema, Partizan Cinema; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where our police station was located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: A technical intervention on my part. Witness, this is all translated simultaneously, if possible, into French and English. This means that you have to wait before answering sometime after Mr. Praljak has stopped his question, otherwise, our poor interpreters cannot follow. Please proceed, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I'm sorry. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes. Let's take it slowly. We have enough time. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The Partizan Cinema Hall is located on the left side of Santiceva Street facing northwards. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And on the opposite side you had the Merkur building; is that right? Well, it was called the Merkur before.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It's the Hit building.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, the Hit building. Now, was your police station on the opposite side as well, or did you have something like that?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Not on the opposite side, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You mean in the Hit building?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, never in the Hit building.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: What was in the Hit building?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It was a department store at one time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: No, we're not speaking about the same thing. You were in the Partizan Cinema Hall. Now, opposite the cinema hall in Santiceva street, what was -- what was there, there on the right-hand side of Santiceva Street looking northwards? Or opposite the Partizan Hall?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: There were residential buildings there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. We won't pursue that line. Now, when you went to work, were you wearing a uniform or not?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon on you or not?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a weapon all the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you go to work by having to cross the Old Bridge or the Tito Bridge or some other bridge?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: It was the Tito Bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right, the Tito Bridge. Now, the Old Bridge during the conflict between the BH army and the HVO, was it used for -- did people cross over wearing uniforms, and did they carry arms across? Is that what it served for?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: The Old Bridge we used for all sorts of purposes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, downstream from that bridge there was the provisional bridge, the Kamenica bridge that was built provisionally by the BH army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And what about that bridge, the Kamenica bridge? Was it used by civilians, soldiers, and everybody else for crossing?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, exclusively civilians, but of course soldiers crossed there too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, do you remember, because a witness told us that here, that there were festivities on the BH army side, they were celebrating, when, with an anti-tank gun, destroyed a tank at Hum hill with a red arrow, as it was called? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you remember another event where a Bofors type 40-millimetre anti-aircraft gun was destroyed, and that was celebrated as a military success? Do you remember that date and that event?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you remember that in September, around the 20th of September, in fact, there was -- well, we can call it a BH army offensive towards Hum hill via Stotina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And the Old Bridge wasn't shot at, at that time, nor was it destroyed. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: You mean in September?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, on that date or before that or -- was the Kamenica bridge targeted in order to be demolished and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, it was targeted, but I can't remember -- it was shot at, but I can't remember, actually, what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's go and look at some photographs. You were in Mostar. Did you ever climb up to the top of Hum hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: But judging by what you were able to see, could you draw the conclusion that if you're up on Hum hill you can see the Old Bridge and Kamenica bridge very well?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course you can see that from Hum hill.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, from Stotina can you see Kamenica as if it was on the palm of your hand?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Before this date, and I'm talking about the 8th of November, did you ever see a tank go out to Stotina and shoot, and fire?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that the HVO had a bunker of some sort at Stotina.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not denying that. Now, can you fit a 20-millimetre PAT gun in a bunker, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, judging by the bunker I saw up at Stotina, I have the feeling that you could get a whole truck in there. A heavy duty vehicle. At least that would be my impression.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right. That's your impression. Fine. But until the 8th of November you never saw a tank go to Stotina and fire at the other side?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Up until the day when I made this footage, you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, they did come, but I just can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You mean a tank came?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Everything came there, not only a tank. Everything did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, when the tank arrived earlier on, what did it fire at from the position of Stotina?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: As far as I can -- am concerned, firing was a regular occurrence and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Don't explain anything to me, Witness, just tell me this: Can you tell me a date before the 8th of November, 1993, that a tank arrived at Stotina, and, if so, then tell me what that tank fired at on that date.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Well, I find it difficult to remember dates generally, but I remember this particular date very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, please focus on my questions. Don't tell me about what I didn't ask you. I'd like us now to take a look at some photographs from 3D 00374. Exhibit 3D 00374 is what I'd like us to look at now. So that we can clarify the situation. It's in the booklet that we all have. On page 48 and 49 you will find four photographs there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English reference [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] 00469.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be easier if the witness had this. Mr. Kovacic, don't you have a copy for the witness? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Certainly he does.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you please go to page 48.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you please look at the first photograph on the left-hand side, the one in the upper half the page.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you see the Old Bridge, and can you agree with me that this photograph was taken from Hum?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: I don't know where it was taken from, but I see the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. You do know that above Old Bridge is the hill of Hum. You do know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at the lower photograph, also taken from Hum hill but with a more general view. The area's under the control of the BH army in Mostar are marked in red. They were marked off. Do you agree that the area marked off in red with some green shadings was under the control of the BH army? The Bulevar and then further down Santiceva Street and back up again. Have a look, please.

utterances.speaker: ENES DELALIC
utterances.text: If we leave aside the hill, you could say that that's it, what I can see here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
